question: Compare current traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the Cape of Good Hope, and explain how oil flows have shifted.
answer: Current traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is about 3 transits per day, down 96% year on year [S7]. In contrast, the Cape of Good Hope has 69 ships per day, down 22% year on year [S5].  Oil flows have shifted from the Strait of Hormuz to the Cape of Good Hope. Before the 2026 war, the Strait of Hormuz carried about 20 million barrels of oil per day [S1]. However, after the war, oil flows through the Cape of Good Hope rose from 6.2 mb/d in 2023 to 9.3 mb/d in 2024 [S2].
